sources.title: Income and the Consumer Price Index (CPI)
Adjusting for Inflation
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

claims.statement: Nominal income is money earned without adjusting for price changes.
Real income adjusts nominal income for price changes to express purchasing power relative to a base period.
With fixed dollars, a higher general price level buys fewer goods and services.
Hypothetical monthly income 3000 to 3150 is +5%; price index 100 to108 is +8%; 3150/1.08=2916.6667 base-year dollars; real growth=1.05/1.08-1=-2.7778%.
claims.notes: Not measured current data; taxes and household spending differences outside scope. 5%-8% is only an approximation, not the exact result.
